claim.title: Ridge Dominates Min-Norm
claim.statement: In the isotropic well-specified and misspecified settings, optimally-tuned ridge regression (minimizing risk over λ) achieves a lower prediction risk than min-norm least squares (λ=0) for all values of γ and SNR.
claim.test_plan: Simulate isotropic model (well-specified) and misspecified model. For γ in [0.5, 1.5, 3.0], compute risk for min-norm (λ=0) and for ridge regression with λ optimized via grid search over [1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 0.1, 1.0]. Pass if min_λ Risk(λ) < Risk(λ=0) for all γ and both model types.
claim.success_criterion: The minimum risk over the ridge penalty grid is strictly less than the min-norm risk for all tested γ values.

feedback: Transferred from the arxiv-1912.07242 audit round: Monte-Carlo audits at d=1000 timed out 3x within the 20-min bound; d<=300 (T<=300 trials, focused grids around critical points) gave statistically clean verdicts in minutes. Design for that envelope. Asymptotic closed-forms converge quickly in d — a large-d run is wasted budget, not better evidence.
